parts.prompt: Contrast what happens to RAM and ROM data after power is removed.
State one operating-system task involving hardware.
Give one practical benefit of compressing a folder before sharing.
Explain how a team can use tracked edits to approve changes in a report.
State two different places to store a backup outside the computer’s internal drive.
A sports watch synchronises with a nearby phone, while the phone accesses maps across town. Identify an appropriate wireless technology for each.
Describe how encryption protects a file sent through a public network.
Explain the meaning of digital footprint using one example from an online classroom.
An unknown account threatens a student in a class discussion. Give two safe responses.
A rule highlights values greater than or equal to 70. For 68, 70, 74 and 69, identify the highlighted values.
Explain whether removing conditional formatting also removes the values in the cells.
A school models lunch demand using the same number of diners daily. State two important inputs.
The model ignores students on a field trip. Explain one possible prediction error and one sensible improvement.
Identify the types of 12, 12.5 and "12".
Explain the difference between = and ==.
Explain what script mode offers compared with typing one command at a time.
State the outputs of print(17 // 5), print(17 % 5), and print(3 * (2 + 4)).
Explain two features of a system that learns to recognise hand gestures from many labelled examples.
Distinguish a simulation from performing the same test in the real world.
A game adjusts opponent difficulty based on player performance. Give one benefit and one potential limitation.

questions.title: School recycling drive spreadsheet
questions.intro: The student council compares mass collected by two houses. B2=35, B3=28, B5=19 and B6=16 (kilograms). B4, B7 and B8 are calculated.

parts.prompt: For a table showing item name, collected kilograms and total kilograms, identify one label, one data value and one calculation.
Collections B2=35 and B3=28; collections B5=19 and B6=16. Write a SUM formula in B4 for B2:B3.
Write a SUM formula in B7 for B5:B6.
Write a formula in B8 for the difference B4 minus B7.
Calculate B8.
A new collection raises B6 by 9 kg. State the new B8 and the amount of change.
A warning displays if B8 is below 20 kg. Write the condition and state what happens at exactly 20.
Two collection plans predict differences of 18 kg and 25 kg. The target is a difference of at least 20 kg. Evaluate the plans using the target, one assumption and a recommendation.
Name the symbols used for Start/Stop, input/output and processing.
An algorithm inputs boxes=6 and books_per_box=9, then outputs boxes * books_per_box. State the process calculation and output.
Trace a different algorithm: Input length=11, width=4, calculate perimeter=2*(length+width), output perimeter. Give final value and output.
Describe a complete sequential flowchart that inputs adults and children, calculates total tickets needed and outputs it. Include the right symbols and correct flow.
A program should compute the cost of 5 passes at $4 each, but uses total = 5 + 4. Identify the error and correct the calculation.
Write Python code that inputs the number of crates and items in each crate as integers, calculates the number of items, and prints it.
Provide one valid test input pair, expected output and reason to test it.
Give a suitable data type a camera-based fish classifier receives.
Explain how examples of labelled fish photographs help the classifier.
Contrast a fixed list of fish species with an AI recognition guide.
Identify a privacy concern and matching safeguard when visitors appear in camera frames.
The system often confuses two similar species. Evaluate whether it should replace every human educator. Give a benefit, limitation, mitigation and recommendation.
Give two benefits of testing the guide virtually before relying on it at a busy aquarium.
